notes: No U.S. state breakdown with values was found. Toyota's per-state fact sheets (toyota.com/.../ops-map/us<xx>/state-<name>.pdf) now return 404; the current operations map embeds only counts of dealerships, offices and facilities per state in page code, not visible text, so they were not used. Toyota's U.S. economic studies by the Center for Automotive Research are older (2015 data) and were not used. Plant sites use the 20-F Item 4.D table (employees as of March 31, 2025) where the plant is listed (Toyota City head office, Motomachi, Tahara, Kentucky, Indiana, North Carolina battery, Canada, Guanajuato); Texas, West Virginia, Alabama and Mississippi come from Toyota USA Newsroom facility pages (read Nov 2026, later than FY2025). Plant figures stay in sites, not state values; Kentucky and Alabama each have more than one Toyota site. The U.S. country row is Toyota's own 'Toyota in the U.S.' totals from the Fall 2023 operations map (cumulative investment $39 billion; employment 49,000); the latest country-contribution sheet says '$50B invested since 1986' but that is a 2026 figure. Japan and the four regions are from the FY2025 20-F; the two 'Other' groups have different definitions for employees and production, so they are separate regions. Production is stored as whole units from a table in thousands. Toyota has over 50 overseas manufacturing companies in 27 countries and regions, listed by name on global.toyota without counts per country, so no plants-per-country figure is given.
